headline: Nine times
subhead: GH AND IGF-1 WENT OPPOSITE WAYS
punch: Every one of them is a published experiment.

headline: What kept happening?
body: So across this entire series one thing kept happening, in different laboratories, across different decades, in different species, using completely different experimental designs. | Serum IGF-1 and actual growth came apart. Not once as a fluke that could be dismissed, and not twice. Nine separate times, each one published, and they are worth seeing collected in one place because no single one of them is convincing and all nine together are.

headline: One
body: Growth hormone injected directly into the growth plate of **one tibia** in a rat whose pituitary had been removed, so the animal made none of its own. The other leg received nothing. That leg grew more. | Same animal, same heart, same bloodstream, the same circulating IGF-1 washing past both legs at identical concentration every second of the experiment. Whatever caused the difference, it could not have been in the blood.

headline: Two
body: Block growth hormone with an antiserum raised against the rat's own GH. The growth plate narrowed, the proliferative zone shrank, and the number of chondrocytes synthesising DNA dropped. The growth genuinely broke. | And **circulating IGF-1 was unchanged** throughout: 10.3 against 10.7 nmol/l at 4 days, which is noise. You can break growth without the blood marker registering anything at all.
punch: The marker sat still while the plate shrank.

headline: Three
body: GH shortened the reserve cell cycle to 8 days against IGF-1's 15, shortened the dividing cell cycle to 3 days against 4.5, and beat IGF-1 at every single stage that was measured. | It did all of that **while producing a lower level of circulating IGF-1** than the group given IGF-1 directly. Lower blood number, more growth, same experiment, same animals, same measurements.

headline: Four
body: The same total daily dose of GH, delivered either continuously or as pulses. The continuous arm produced the **higher serum IGF-1** of the two. | And the pulsed arm grew more. Their own summary sentence: receptor, GH-BP and IGF-1 are stimulated more by continuous delivery, whereas growth is enhanced more by pulsatility. The marker and the outcome were driven apart deliberately, by design.
punch: The number and the growth moved apart by design.

headline: Five
body: An IGF-1 protein engineered to bind cartilage and concentrate at the growth plate, and a chemically identical IGF-1 with no targeting. Same molecule, same dose, same animal model, one variable. | The targeted version grew bone. The non-targeted version **showed no significant effect on growth** whatsoever. So the amount of IGF-1 present was never the variable. Where it ended up was.

headline: Six
body: Twenty-four weeks of structured jumping in short-stature children, against two separate untreated control groups. Height rose and serum IGF-1 rose, at p < 0.05. | And serum **GH showed no significant difference** between groups, before or after, at p > 0.05. The downstream hormone moved without the upstream one moving at all, which the standard chain does not permit.

headline: Seven
body: Energy deficit raises GH and lowers IGF-1 simultaneously, because the liver downregulates its GH receptors and stops answering the signal. | Rats fasted for 3 days dropped one tibial growth plate to 30% of control and stopped the other one completely. The GH number was climbing the entire time this was happening.

headline: Eight
body: The same range of GH doses, 0.01 to 0.10 mg/kg/day, produced IGF-1 results above and below the 2 SDS line, with the dose ranges for the two groups overlapping almost completely. | Pubertal stage moves it. Hepatic insulin exposure moves it. Which means that number is a composite of several inputs and only one of them is the dose you took.
punch: One dose, the whole range of numbers.

headline: Nine
body: A family carrying mutations in **NPR2**, the receptor for CNP, which has nothing whatsoever to do with the growth hormone axis. | The member with the full dysplasia had **low IGF-1 and evidence of GH resistance**. A defect in an entirely separate pathway showed up as a growth hormone problem on the bloodwork of someone whose GH axis was fine.
punch: A second pathway, reading out on the first.

headline: So does IGF-1 not matter?
body: It does not mean IGF-1 is unimportant. In most of these experiments IGF-1 is the actual mediator doing the work. The local pool, made inside the plate, is what drives the growth. | What it means is that the serum number is a different thing from the local pool, and it has at least five inputs other than your GH dose feeding into it. Those two facts together are why it keeps going the wrong way.
punch: _Local IGF-1 matters. Serum IGF-1 reports on it badly._

headline: The one line worth keeping
body: If nine experiments across forty years can move your blood marker one direction and your actual growth the other, then that marker is not the thing you are trying to change. | It is one readout, with its own set of confounders, sitting several steps downstream of the process that actually matters to you.
punch: ==Stop grading yourself on a number that has gone the wrong way nine times.==
